clue.text: Prepare to admit first blunder

indicators.note: to admit something is to let it in, so these letters go inside the other word

parts.note: to make a meal is to prepare it
1ST, written as IST, is the ordinal abbreviation for first

explanation.surface: Someone getting ready to own up to an initial mistake.
explanation.walkthrough: IST stands for 1ST, the digit 1 read as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: A mistake and a blunder are both errors, so the words are plain synonyms.

clue.text: A Western invasion of one African country or another

indicators.note: an invasion goes into a place, so these letters are put inside the country's name

parts.note: Mali is a country in West Africa

explanation.surface: A Western power invading some country or other in Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One African country or another' reads as a single vague phrase, but MALI is the first country and the definition is just 'another', a second African country.
explanation.definitionFit: Malawi is a further African country, distinct from Mali, so it is the 'another' of the phrase.

clue.text: Sleep in the cosiest apartment

indicators.note: the answer sits inside the run of letters across the next two words

explanation.surface: Taking a nap in the snuggest flat.
explanation.definitionFit: A siesta is an afternoon nap, a short sleep taken in hot countries.

clue.text: Something not right with helping to chase grizzly bear

indicators.note: to chase is to come after, so this piece follows the anagram
grizzly can mean grumpy or messed up, telling us to rearrange the word bear

parts.note: the fodder for the anagram
a ration is a helping or portion of food

explanation.surface: Something wrong with a portion of food that a grizzly bear is pursuing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grizzly bear' reads as the animal, but 'grizzly' here means messed up and is the signal to rearrange the following word.
explanation.definitionFit: An aberration is a departure from what is normal or correct.

clue.text: Gatekeeper won't begin to show the way in

indicators.note: the word refuses to start, so its first letter is dropped

parts.note: a sentry guards a gate or entrance

explanation.surface: A gatekeeper refusing to start pointing out the entrance.
explanation.definitionFit: An entry is an entrance, a door or passage by which one goes into a place.

clue.text: Nice sea colour, one might say, appearing first in rose?

indicators.note: the sounded colour comes before the next piece
this signals that a word is to be read by its sound

parts.note: blue is a colour, said aloud as BLOO
mer is French for sea, and Nice is a French city

explanation.surface: Describing the colour of the Mediterranean at Nice, seen first in a rose.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nice' is the French city, not the adjective, so the sea is French: MER. The question mark marks a rose as only one example of the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A bloomer is a flowering plant, and a rose is one such flower.

clue.text: Wobbling shapely bum? Heartless and an unacceptable thing to say

indicators.note: wobbling suggests unsteady movement, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: part of the anagram fodder

indicators.note: without its heart, the middle letter of the word goes

parts.note: the word whose middle is removed

explanation.surface: A rude remark about a jiggling curvy backside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heartless' takes the U from BUM, leaving BM; those letters go in with SHAPELY and are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Blasphemy is speech insulting to God or sacred things, the classic forbidden utterance.

clue.text: Lovers remove clothing and cheat, but not starting to get too excited

indicators.note: taking the clothes off strips the outside, leaving the middle letters

parts.note: the word whose outer letters are stripped

indicators.note: not starting means the first letter is dropped

parts.note: the word that loses its first letter

explanation.surface: Lovers undressing and being unfaithful, getting overheated.
explanation.definitionFit: To overheat is to become too hot, figuratively to become overexcited or agitated.

clue.text: Road race 21

parts.note: the M1 motorway, written MI in crosswords, is a well-known British road
a sprint is a short fast race

explanation.surface: Reads as a cross-reference, a road race named after another clue.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition points at 21 across, TYPO. The M1 is England's main north-south motorway.
explanation.definitionFit: A misprint is a printing error, which is exactly what a typo is.

clue.text: Introducing dodgy equipment at first to working nurses shows disrespect

indicators.note: introducing one thing to another puts it inside
working suggests something being worked over, so the letters of nurses are rearranged

parts.note: the anagram fodder

indicators.note: the first letters of the two preceding words

explanation.surface: Bringing faulty kit into a ward where nurses are on duty is insolent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at first' takes D and E from dodgy equipment; these go into an arrangement of NURSES.
explanation.definitionFit: Rudeness is impolite behaviour, a lack of respect shown to others.

clue.text: Lord, say, implicated in falsehood

indicators.note: to be implicated in something is to be caught up inside it

parts.note: a lie is a falsehood
EG, for example, is what say means here

explanation.surface: A nobleman, for example, mixed up in a lie.
explanation.definitionFit: A liege is a feudal lord to whom service is owed.

clue.text: Came across Ted welcoming partygoers

indicators.note: to welcome someone is to take them in, so the other piece goes inside

parts.note: ravers are people who go to wild parties

explanation.surface: Someone called Ted was met while letting party people in.
explanation.definitionFit: To traverse is to travel across, so traversed means went across.

clue.text: Daphne's hen party planned with film crew at the end

definitions.note: Daphne is, in Greek myth, a naiad, so the definition reads Daphne is one

indicators.note: a party being planned is being arranged, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the main anagram fodder

indicators.note: the last letters of the two preceding words

explanation.surface: A woman named Daphne's bachelorette party, organised with a film crew at the end.
explanation.walkthrough: A hen party is a British bride's pre-wedding party for women. 'at the end' gives M and W from film crew. In Greek myth Daphne was a naiad, a river nymph turned into a laurel.
explanation.definitionFit: Daphne is a figure from Greek mythology who was a naiad, a freshwater spirit.

clue.text: First newspaper of record is back in press

indicators.note: back tells us to read the collected letters backwards
the first letters of the four following words

explanation.surface: The leading paper of record returns to printing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'newspaper of record' looks like a single phrase; really only initials are wanted: N, O, R, I, which read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To iron clothes is to press them smooth with a hot flat implement.

clue.text: Modern teething result went first

parts.note: teething produces a new fang, a new tooth
led means went in front

explanation.surface: A recent case where teething came out on top.
explanation.definitionFit: Newfangled describes something novel and modern, often disapprovingly.

clue.text: Bleat about return of evil after X game

indicators.note: this piece comes after the ten
about suggests turning around, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the anagram fodder
X is ten in Roman numerals

indicators.note: a return goes back the way it came, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: sin is evil

explanation.surface: A complaint about wickedness coming back after some X-rated game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' rearranges BLEAT into TABLE; then TEN for X, then SIN read backwards as NIS.
explanation.definitionFit: Table tennis, or ping-pong, is an indoor bat-and-ball game.

clue.text: Soldier's beer drinking exploit with Elizabeth the first

definitions.note: the definition reads 'Soldier is', describing the answer

indicators.note: drinking takes something in, so these letters go inside the word beer

parts.note: a feat is an exploit, a daring deed

indicators.note: the first letter of Elizabeth

explanation.surface: A soldier's beer, taken alongside a heroic deed in the time of Queen Elizabeth I.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Elizabeth the first' reads as the Tudor queen, but only the first letter, E, is wanted. Beefeaters are the Yeoman Warders guarding the Tower of London.
explanation.definitionFit: A Beefeater is a Yeoman Warder, a ceremonial guard drawn from army veterans.

clue.text: Laughing in these, slip, running?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to be laughing uncontrollably
second meaning: slip stitch and running stitch are kinds of ... in sewing

explanation.walkthrough: 'slip' and 'running' look like a fall and a race, but both are sewing stitch names.
explanation.definitionFit: Stitches are both sharp pains from laughing and the individual loops of thread in needlework.

clue.text: Led with this rock band flyer

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the British rock band
second meaning: an airship that flies

explanation.surface: A rock band leading with a flying machine.
explanation.definitionFit: A zeppelin is a rigid airship, so it is something that flies.

clue.text: Yes, doctor: from here, operating theatre work

indicators.note: operating suggests working on something, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A doctor agreeing to start surgery from this point in the operating theatre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'operating theatre' looks like one hospital phrase, but 'operating' is the anagram signal and 'theatre work' the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The Comedy of Errors is a Shakespeare play, a dramatic work for the stage.

clue.text: Get even with travel agency management centres

indicators.note: the centres are the middle letters of each of the three preceding words

explanation.surface: Taking revenge on a travel firm's bosses.
explanation.definitionFit: To avenge a wrong is to retaliate for it, settling the score.

clue.text: See 18
The Grauniad may be involved in party politics

definitions.note: the Guardian is nicknamed the Grauniad because of its reputation for printing errors

indicators.note: the answer sits within the letters of the next two words

explanation.surface: The Guardian newspaper may get caught up in political party affairs.
explanation.walkthrough: The Grauniad is a jokey misspelling of the Guardian, a British newspaper famous for errors.
explanation.definitionFit: A typo is a typing error, the very kind of slip that earned the paper its nickname.

clue.text: I'm surprised to be truly engaged, always

parts.note: well can mean truly, as in well worth it
in can mean engaged or occupied, as in in use
ever means always

explanation.surface: Astonishment at being really engaged forever.
explanation.definitionFit: Well I never is an exclamation of astonishment.

clue.text: End of chapel and end of church showing gap

indicators.note: the last letter of the word chapel

parts.note: the apse is the rounded east end of a church

explanation.surface: The far end of a chapel and of a church revealing a space.
explanation.walkthrough: 'end of' appears twice but does different jobs: the first picks a final letter, the second is a whole architectural feature.
explanation.definitionFit: A lapse is an interval or break in time, a gap.

clue.text: See 6
In dance, change one type of shirt for another, more revealing

indicators.note: these letters go in the dance word

parts.note: a hop is an informal dance
to alter is to change
a T-shirt is one type of shirt

explanation.surface: At a dance, swapping one shirt for something more daring.
explanation.definitionFit: A halter top is a garment tied behind the neck, leaving the back and shoulders bare.

clue.text: 'Glo', so to speak?

parts.note: putting L inside the word GO produces G-L-O, so the clue word is what that wordplay would give

explanation.surface: Glo, as people might say it.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue works backwards: Glo is what you get by putting L in GO. 'Speak' is a noun here, as in jargon names ending -speak.
explanation.definitionFit: Lingo is a particular jargon or way of talking, as '-speak' means in words like newspeak.

clue.text: No good reason to accept Tory leader as a politician

indicators.note: the rearranged reason is to take in the extra letter, which sits inside it
no good means faulty, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the main anagram fodder

indicators.note: the leader of the word Tory is its first letter

explanation.surface: A useless argument for accepting the head of the Conservatives as a politician.
explanation.walkthrough: A Tory is a member of Britain's Conservative Party; only its first letter is wanted, and it goes inside SENAOR, the letters of reason after 'No good' rearranges them.
explanation.definitionFit: A senator is a member of a senate, an elected lawmaker.

clue.text: Steel bands bat out composition like Schubert's 8th symphony?

indicators.note: out means the letters of bat are to be taken away
a composition is something put together, so the remaining letters are arranged

parts.note: the letters removed from the fodder

explanation.surface: Steel bands playing a musical arrangement in the style of Schubert's eighth.
explanation.walkthrough: Schubert's 8th is known as the Unfinished Symphony, so it is playfully described as having no end.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unfinished never reaches its conclusion, so it can be jokingly called without end.
